config.title: Token Refresh with Axios Interceptor

intro.title: Token Refresh with Axios Interceptor
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a secure Vue application that automatically refreshes an expired authentication token using Axios interceptors. You will learn how to intercept HTTP requests and responses to check for token expiration and handle refresh logic seamlessly. The core programming concept involves using Axios interceptors to manage API calls and asynchronous token refresh without disrupting the user experience. You will work with Vue's composition API, Axios for HTTP requests, and JavaScript promises to implement this common real-world security pattern.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential in any web application that requires persistent user authentication, such as admin dashboards, e-commerce platforms, or collaborative tools like project management software. For example, while a user is actively working in a dashboard viewing analytics or filling out a lengthy form, their access token may expire. An interceptor silently refreshes the token in the background, preventing disruptive logout modals or form submission errors. This provides a seamless, professional user experience, ensuring uninterrupted interaction with critical UI components like data tables, editors, or real-time notification panels.

objectives: Initialize an Axios instance with a base URL for API requests
Configure an Axios request interceptor to attach authorization tokens to outgoing requests
Implement an Axios response interceptor to detect expired token errors (401)
Construct a token refresh function that calls the refresh endpoint and updates stored tokens
Integrate token refresh logic into the response interceptor to retry failed requests
Control request queuing during token refresh to prevent duplicate refresh calls
Apply the configured Axios instance to Vue components for making authenticated API calls

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add request interceptor to attach access token
steps.instruction: Add a request interceptor to your axios instance that attaches the current access token to the Authorization header of outgoing requests.
steps.hint: Use the .interceptors.request.use() method on your axios instance. The interceptor function should modify the request config headers before the request is sent.
steps.expectedOutcome: The axios instance will have a request interceptor that automatically adds the Authorization header with the current access token value to all outgoing requests.
successCriteria: A request interceptor is added using .interceptors.request.use() that sets config.headers.Authorization with the accessToken ref value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your interceptor function properly modifies the config.headers.Authorization property and returns the config object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The request interceptor wasn't properly implemented. Check that you're using .interceptors.request.use() on your axios instance and modifying the request config headers.

steps.title: Add response interceptor to handle token refresh
steps.instruction: Add a response interceptor to your axiosInstance that checks for 401 status codes and triggers a token refresh.
steps.hint: Use axiosInstance.interceptors.response.use() to add the interceptor. The first callback handles successful responses, the second handles errors. Check if error.response.status equals 401.
steps.expectedOutcome: The axiosInstance will have a response interceptor that detects 401 errors, though the actual refresh logic will be added in later steps.
successCriteria: A response interceptor is added to axiosInstance that checks for 401 status codes in error responses.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a response interceptor, but make sure it properly checks for 401 status codes using error.response?.status === 401.
steps.feedbackWrong: The response interceptor wasn't added correctly. Remember to use axiosInstance.interceptors.response.use() with both success and error callbacks.
